basics.name: Deyan Dobrinov
basics.label: Development lead at Dext
basics.summary: I am a software developer with more than 14 years of professional experience. In the past several years I am mostly working on Ruby/Rails web projects. I believe that every complex problem has a simple solution, which could be found if you understand where the complexity comes from. I enjoy doing that. I like good UX, and I fight for it.

headline: I find the simple solution hiding inside complex systems.

facts.label: shipping software, since 2007. 15 of them before AI coding tools.

engineering.name: Making complex systems simple
engineering.proof: Search rebuilt on Elasticsearch · a monolith split into a service
engineering.detail: At Dext, replaced an over-complex PostgreSQL search with Elasticsearch, so the app became a thin layer around a search engine. Extracted manual data extraction from the monolith into its own service through incremental releases.

engineering.name: Shipping risky change safely
engineering.proof: Front-end rewrite with no incremental release, team of 8
engineering.detail: Moved Dext’s main app to React + TypeScript on a new GraphQL API and rolled it out with a low amount of risk.

engineering.name: Financial documents and data
engineering.proof: OCR tables, bank statements, invoices · P2P lending
engineering.detail: Table extraction from OCR data, transaction and line-item flows and PDF splitting at Dext. Technical-debt work at Funding Circle, a peer-to-peer lending platform.

engineering.name: Leading and mentoring
engineering.proof: Teams of up to 8 · can mentor 14 technologies
engineering.detail: Team lead for 2 engineers and 1 QA, then development lead reporting to the CTO. Can mentor in Ruby, Rails, TypeScript, React, GraphQL, PostgreSQL and 8 more.

highlights.title: A front-end rewrite with no incremental release
highlights.hook: Led 8 people moving Dext’s main app to React, TypeScript and GraphQL, then shipped it in one go.
highlights.problem: Dext’s main application needed a new front-end stack, and a big part of it had to be rewritten. Incremental releases were not possible.
highlights.did: Led a team of 8. We rewrote a large part of the app in React + TypeScript on a newly created GraphQL API.
highlights.outcome: Rolled out with a low amount of risk.

highlights.title: Reading tables out of OCR with simple maths
highlights.hook: Before LLMs could read invoices, I found rows and columns by overlaying OCR data on the image.
highlights.problem: Line items and bank transactions had to be extracted more efficiently. That data usually sits in tables.
highlights.did: Overlaid OCR data on the document image so people could select it, then used simple mathematics to recognise the rows and columns.
highlights.outcome: Rows and columns were recognised automatically, so line items and bank transactions could be extracted from tables.

highlights.title: Carpass: built for my car, used by 3000+ people
highlights.hook: Built a vehicle maintenance log alone and kept it running from 2016 to 2020.
highlights.problem: I needed a tool to log the maintenance history of my car.
highlights.did: Designed, built and ran it alone, next to a full-time job, for over four years.

projects.name: JsonMe
projects.description: JsonMe is a web application allowing software engineers to maintain a resume in json format and keep it in their Github/Gitlab profile. The CV that you are looking at the moment is generated with it.

projects.name: Textstandup
projects.description: Web application for text based stand-ups. I was not happy with the efficiency of the stand-up meetings so I started doing them in a text form in my team. This was working well so I wrote a web application for this. More about the motivation behind the project could be found here - https://medium.com/@ddobrinov/text-based- stand-ups-de741fa6c724.
